steps.body: Pair things up to compare! Line up cats and mats. Extra cats left over? Then cats are **more**.

widget.prompt: 5 cats, 3 mats. Every cat wants a mat. Are there more cats or more mats? Tap the group with more.

hotspots.label: 3 mats
hotspots.feedback: Pair them up: 2 cats are LEFT OVER, so cats are more.

widget.missFeedback: Two cats have no mat — cats are more.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 2 cats have no mat, so cats are more.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents more fewer.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for more fewer must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines more fewer.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: **Fewer** means not as many. 3 mats and 5 cats: mats are **fewer**.

explanationVariants: Pair the 4 spoons with the 6 bowls: 2 bowls have no spoon, so spoons are fewer.
4 is not as many as 6 — spoons are fewer.

widget.prompt: There are 6 bowls and 4 spoons. Which is fewer? Tap the group with fewer.

hotspots.label: 6 bowls
hotspots.feedback: Bowls are MORE (6). Spoons (4) are fewer.

widget.missFeedback: Pair them: 2 bowls miss a spoon, so spoons are fewer.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 4 spoons is not as many as 6 bowls.

misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines more fewer.

widget.prompt: One frame shows 6. Tap dots to make this frame show 6 too.

commonCounts.feedback: One fewer than the other frame. Add 1 more.
One too many. Equal means the SAME: 6.

widget.successFeedback: Equal! Both frames show 6 — the same amount.

predict.prompt: The other frame shows 6. To make yours EQUAL, you need…
predict.reveal: Equal means the very same count — 6 and 6, no more, no fewer. One extra dot or one missing dot breaks the tie.

cml.actionGoal: Build the quantity in a structured frame, then reorganize it without recounting every object.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Move the counters into a different arrangement that still shows the same number. What must not change?

explanation.prompt: Why can the counters move without changing the answer?

options.label: The arrangement can change while the number of counters stays fixed.
options.feedback: Exactly. Quantity is preserved when only the arrangement changes.

options.label: The answer changes whenever the picture looks different.
options.feedback: That describes a surface feature, not the mathematical relationship that must remain true. Quantity is preserved when only the arrangement changes.

explanationVariants: 7 pencils and 7 crayons pair up perfectly — no leftovers means equal.

widget.prompt: There are 7 pencils and 7 crayons. Which is true?

options.label: More pencils
options.feedback: They pair up exactly — 7 and 7 are EQUAL.

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Yes — every pencil pairs with a crayon, none left over.

explanationVariants: Pair 8 birds with 5 nests: 3 birds have no nest, so birds are more.
8 is more than 5 — leftover birds show it.

widget.prompt: 8 birds, 5 nests. Which is more? Tap the group with more.

hotspots.label: 5 nests
hotspots.feedback: Nests run out first — BIRDS are more (8 vs 5).

widget.missFeedback: 3 birds have no nest, so the groups are NOT equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 3 birds are left without a nest, so birds are more.

explanationVariants: Count each: 4 cars, 6 balls, 5 tops. The 6 balls are the most.
6 is more than 5 and more than 4 — balls win.

widget.prompt: Toys on a shelf: 4 cars, 6 balls, 5 tops. Which group has the MOST? Tap it.

hotspots.label: 4 cars
hotspots.feedback: 4 is the FEWEST — the most is 6 balls.

hotspots.label: 5 tops
hotspots.feedback: 5 is close, but 6 balls is more.

widget.missFeedback: The counts differ: 4, 6, 5 — balls (6) are most.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 6 beats 5 and 4. Balls are the most.

hints: The biggest count is the most: 6 balls.

steps.body: Pair up to compare. Leftovers mean more; not enough means fewer.
takeaways: Pair things up to compare groups.
Leftovers mean that group has more.

concept.body: Pair things up to compare. Leftovers mean more. Not enough means fewer. Exact match means equal.

explanationVariants: 3 hats and 5 heads: 2 heads have no hat, so hats are fewer.
3 is not as many as 5 — fewer hats.

widget.prompt: There are 5 heads and 3 hats. Which is fewer?

options.label: Hats
options.feedback: Yes — 3 hats is not as many as 5 heads.

options.label: Heads
options.feedback: Heads are MORE (5). Hats (3) are fewer.

options.label: The same
options.feedback: 2 heads have no hat — not equal. Hats are fewer.

options.label: Neither
options.feedback: 3 is fewer than 5 — hats are fewer.
